440: My boat is small. The ships are enormous. Somehow I am in charge, and it surprises me daily.
441: I push things a hundred times my size. My little boat has never once complained. I complain plenty.
442: People see a giant ship move and assume it decided to. No. That was me, and my very small boat.
443: The ship weighs more than a mountain. I nudge it politely and hope very much for the best.
444: My entire career is convincing enormous things to move slightly to the left.
445: I have the smallest boat in the harbor and the largest responsibilities in it. It works, mostly.
446: A ship this big has no idea where the harbor entrance is. Luckily, one very small boat knows exactly.
447: I spend my days pushing something that could crush me, very slowly, and with great affection.
448: A ship this size cannot stop quickly. So mostly my job is starting to stop it long before anyone thinks we should.
449: Push too hard and the ship swings the wrong way. So I push almost gently, and apologize quietly when I do not.
450: People wave at the giant ship. Nobody waves at the little boat doing all the work. I wave back anyway.
451: My boat is tiny and stubborn. Between the two of us, the stubborn part does most of the actual work.
452: I once pushed a ship so long that by the time the front reached the dock, the back was still thinking about it.
453: The trick is patience. You cannot rush something that big. Believe me, over the years I have tried.
454: My job is being small and confident next to something huge and helpless. We truly need each other.
455: I spend hours moving a ship a short distance. It is the most important short distance in the harbor.
456: A giant vessel, a tiny boat, and me in the middle, quietly steering the whole disagreement.
457: People underestimate small boats. So do the big ships, right up until the moment I push them.
458: I do not fight the big ships. I lean on them, gently, until they finally agree to go where I want.
459: My boat is little. My determination is not. That, honestly, is the entire job.
460: I know four phrases. I use all four constantly. It has served me beautifully so far.
461: I heard something. I will now repeat it to everyone, forever. This is my job. I adore my job.
462: I want a cracker. I wanted one before you arrived. I will want one long after you leave.
463: I sit on a shoulder and repeat what people say. Nobody tells me secrets anymore. I cannot imagine why.
464: I have strong opinions and one tiny beak. Both of them are extremely loud.
465: The sailors lower their voices whenever I am near. It never helps. My hearing is the best thing about me.
466: I only know a few words, but I say each one at maximum volume. Also, I would like a cracker.
467: People think I do not understand them. I understand plenty. I simply choose to shout it back.
468: I repeat the gossip whether or not it is true. Accuracy was never part of my job description.
469: I have sat on this shoulder for years. I have heard everything. I have kept none of it to myself.
470: Give me a cracker and I will tell you nothing useful, loudly, and with tremendous confidence.
471: I know exactly three things, and I am wrong about one of them. I will not tell you which.
472: The captain keeps telling me to be quiet. The captain does not seem to know who is truly in charge here.
473: I repeat what I hear. If you did not want it repeated, you should not have said it near a bird.
474: I have opinions about the weather, the food, and you specifically. Mostly about the cracker situation.
475: Everyone thinks the parrot is decoration. The parrot heard what you said last night. The parrot remembers.
476: I say the same phrase a hundred times a day. It is a good phrase. Why change something that works.
477: I would tell you a secret, but first, and this part is important, I am going to need a cracker.
478: I am small, I am loud, and I know things. It is a dangerous combination, and I enjoy every part of it.
479: They taught me polite words. I use them to spread gossip. On the whole, a very fair trade.
